classification.difficultyReason: Combines equal-side markings, triangle and special-quadrilateral properties, and supplementary angles in composite figures.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals.

spec.description: An unshaded rhombus adjoining a right triangle, with a continuous horizontal baseline, four matching equality ticks, angle arcs labelled e, f, g and h, a 27° given and a right-angle marker.
spec.mathematics: The rhombus's lower-right interior angle and the triangle's 27° angle are supplementary. Opposite rhombus angles are equal and adjacent rhombus angles are supplementary.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and pronumerals appear; calculated values are answer-controlled.

answer.worked:
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}e+27^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\e&=153^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
The four equal sides identify a rhombus. Opposite angles are equal, so $f=153^{\circ}$. Adjacent angles are supplementary.
$$\begin{align*}g+153^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\g&=27^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Opposite angles are equal, so $h=27^{\circ}$.

spec.description: An unshaded isosceles triangle adjoining an isosceles trapezium. The triangle's upper side continues straight through the upper shared vertex; three sides have matching equality ticks, two opposite trapezium sides have matching parallel arrows, and the angle arcs show 26°, d and e.
spec.mathematics: The triangle's two base angles are 26°, giving its remaining angle as 128°. The straight continuation makes d supplementary to 128°. The parallel sides and equal legs identify an isosceles trapezium, whose lower base angles are 128°.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and pronumerals appear; calculated values are answer-controlled.

answer.worked:
The triangle has two equal sides, so its other base angle is $26^{\circ}$. Let its angle at the upper shared vertex be $t$.
$$\begin{align*}t+26^{\circ}+26^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\t+52^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\t&=128^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}d+128^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\d&=52^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
The quadrilateral is an isosceles trapezium. Its upper base angles are equal, and angles along either leg are supplementary.
$$\begin{align*}e+52^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\e&=128^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
